description: Dependency updates run unattended: Renovate opens the PR, CI gates it, GitHub merges it. `ci.yml` (rustfmt, clippy, cargo deny, cargo audit, cargo test, wasm-pack build, wasm-pack test) is what stands between an automerge and a bad dependency, so every one of those jobs is a required check on `development`.

The Cargo ranges in Cargo.toml are minimums ('1.0', '0.4'), so the cargo manager's default rangeStrategy resolves to update-lockfile: most crate updates change Cargo.lock only. That is the intended shape — the manifest says what the crate needs, the lock says what it was built and tested against — but it means the PR diff is usually a lock file, and the CI jobs above are what actually read it.

Updates are held for three days after release (`minimumReleaseAge`). This crate is published to npm as a wasm module, so a dependency that lands here ends up inside bundles other people ship; three days is the window in which a compromised or broken release is normally yanked.
schedule: before 5am on the 1st and 15th day of the month

packageRules.description: wasm-bindgen and its satellites are version-locked against each other and against the wasm-bindgen CLI wasm-pack runs; bumping one alone produces a module that fails to instantiate.

A wasm-pack bump changes the generated JS glue and the module's bytes, which is the one dependency update that should be looked at rather than merged on a green suite. Same for the wasm-bindgen family it is locked against: `wasm-pack test --headless --chrome` can pass on a pair that still misbehaves in a consumer's bundler.

schedule: before 5am on the 1st day of the month

customManagers.description: WASM_PACK_VERSION is pinned in the workflows because wasm-pack decides the generated bindings. A pin nobody updates is how it ends up back on `latest`, so Renovate owns it.
